y-m-08-03.title: Join squares using wooden sticks
y-m-08-03.topic: Rule for shape pattern (stick count growth)
y-m-08-03.goal: See predictions differ with two data vs more; explain stick growth from how shapes join.
y-m-08-03.material: Join same-size squares in one row with sticks. One square uses 4; neighbors share one stick. Only side by side.
y-m-08-03.thinking.0: Predict with little data and confidence
y-m-08-03.s.s1.prompt: Look at data one step at a time and predict stick total.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.hint.0: Pair square counts and stick counts already seen.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.hint.1: How many new sticks when add one square?
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.0.ask: How many sticks for 3 joined squares?
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.0.after: 4 for 1 and 7 for 2 fit rule +3. But two data points allow other rules, so test 3 squares to gain confidence.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.0.r.a: This use increase between two data and continue.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.0.r.b: This miss neighboring squares share a stick.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Two points no reason to assume increase changes.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.0.o.d: Only two data, can't be sure, but 10 most likely.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.0.r.d: This predicts while remembering data small.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.1.info: You check 3 squares need 10 sticks, 4 need 13.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.1.ask: If 10 squares in one row, how many sticks total?
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.1.after: Starting at 4, add 3 each new square. To get 10, add 3 nine times: 4 plus nine 3s. 9
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.1.r.a: This count 4 sticks per square, no subtract shared ones.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.1.r.b: This count starting 4, then add the increment each time.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.1.r.c: This multiply number squares by increment; check starting 4.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Number of increments from 13 may differ.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.2.info: There are 30 sticks. Join squares same row. You don't need use all, just no shortage. Max squares?
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.2.ask: You don't need use all sticks, just don't run short. What is maximum square count?
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.2.after: 9 squares need 28; 10 need 31. With 30 make 9 and 2 leftover. This uses rule backward to find limit.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.2.r.a: This divide 30 treating each square as 4 sticks.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.2.r.b: This divide 30 by increase 3. What about first 4 sticks?
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.2.r.c: Maybe guess close by feel. Find sticks for 8 and 9 squares.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.st.2.r.d: This find stick count for each square number and largest ≤30.
y-m-08-03.s.s1.reflect: At first predict from 2 data, then check as data grew. Finally use rule backward for new question. Review how confidence change.
y-m-08-03.s.s2.prompt: Choose expressions correctly giving sticks for 10 joined squares.
y-m-08-03.s.s2.hint.0: For each expression, see if calculated value 31.
y-m-08-03.s.s2.hint.1: Substitute 2 squares in each and check gives 7 sticks. 2
y-m-08-03.s.s2.r.a: This count 4 for each square. What about shared sticks?
y-m-08-03.s.s2.r.b: This count first square separately from additions.
y-m-08-03.s.s2.r.c: This puts 3 per square and adds starting stick.
y-m-08-03.s.s2.r.d: This treats 7 as bundle for two squares. Consider shared sticks between bundles.
y-m-08-03.s.s2.r.e: This counts 4 per square then subtracts double-counted sticks.
y-m-08-03.s.s2.explain: Three expressions give 31: 4+3×9 (first 4 plus nine increases), 3×10+1 (3 per square plus initial 1), 4×10−9 (subtract 9 shared sticks). 4×10 and 7×5 fail to subtract shared sticks. 3 4
y-m-08-03.s.s3.prompt: Explain why adding one square needs 3 new sticks, not 4.
y-m-08-03.s.s3.hint.0: Say where stick placed when joining two squares.
y-m-08-03.s.s3.hint.1: Count how many of 4 sides newly placed.
y-m-08-03.s.s3.selfAssess.0: You mention how many sides touch neighboring square?
y-m-08-03.s.s3.selfAssess.1: You connect to square has 4 sides?
y-m-08-03.s.s3.selfAssess.2: You check using explanation that 2 to 3 squares changes 7 to 10?
y-m-08-03.s.s3.model.0: New square has 4 sides, but one touches previous square, sharing a stick. So only 3 new sticks.
y-m-08-03.s.s3.model.1: When you attach square, one stick shared, so only 3 new needed, not 4.

y-m-08-08.title: Kidney bean height: same after 10 weeks?
y-m-08-08.topic: When rule can extend far into future
y-m-08-08.goal: Check if rule from 3 weeks' records can be extended as-is through 10 weeks, and what extra data makes prediction more trustworthy.
y-m-08-08.material:
Seohyeon measure sprout same day each week. Water/sunlight same. Unit cm.
Week | After 1 week | After 2 weeks | After 3 weeks
Height | 3 | 6 | 9
Seohyeon says, "It grows 3cm each week, so after 10 weeks it will be 30cm."
y-m-08-08.thinking.2: Compare new records and find overreach
y-m-08-08.s.s1.prompt: What is right about Seohyeon prediction?
y-m-08-08.s.s1.hint.0: Put recorded weeks and predicted week side by side.
y-m-08-08.s.s1.hint.1: Write what known about weeks outside recorded range.
y-m-08-08.s.s1.o.a: After 10 weeks, it definitely be 30cm following 3-week rule
y-m-08-08.s.s1.r.a: This carry 3-week data straight through 10 and become certain.
y-m-08-08.s.s1.o.b: After 10 weeks, it definitely differ from 3-week rule, so not 30cm
y-m-08-08.s.s1.r.b: This state rule wrong without basis; no evidence it changes yet.
y-m-08-08.s.s1.o.c: From 3 weeks alone, can't decide 10-week height is 30cm
y-m-08-08.s.s1.r.c: This separate data range and prediction range.
y-m-08-08.s.s1.o.d: If it keeps growing 3cm weekly, after 10 weeks 30cm
y-m-08-08.s.s1.r.d: This predict with condition rule continues.
y-m-08-08.s.s1.explain: 3 weeks at 3cm each no guarantee 30 after 10. Conditional statement "if it keeps growing 3cm, then 30" okay. Need more records to check condition.
y-m-08-08.s.s1.acc.0: This prediction includes continuing rule condition. Better also say condition unverified.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.prompt: You want more trustworthy 10-week height prediction. Choose everything helpful.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.hint.0: Compare what tells more about future week: existing or not-yet-existing records.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.hint.1: For each choice, say if you learn anything new about week 10.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.o.a: Record whether it keeps growing 3cm after weeks 4 and 5
y-m-08-08.s.s2.r.a: This tests whether rule continues with future records.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.r.b: This examines existing records; no new info on unmeasured weeks.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.o.c: Find roughly usual fully grown kidney bean height
y-m-08-08.s.s2.o.d: Ask friends for guesses and follow majority
y-m-08-08.s.s2.r.d: Majority guess no change actual height.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.o.e: Collect records from other beans under same conditions
y-m-08-08.s.s2.r.e: This checks rule using several examples.
y-m-08-08.s.s2.explain: Records close to prediction (weeks 4,5), other same-condition beans, and normal full-grown height add basis. Rechecking old data or following majority adds no basis. 4 5
y-m-08-08.s.s3.prompt: Seohyeon grew bean and measured 11cm at week4, 12cm week5. Here's summary. Choose line hard to believe.
y-m-08-08.s.s3.hint.0: From 11 at week4 and 12 at week5, find increase each week.
y-m-08-08.s.s3.hint.1: Separate lines confirmed by record from lines extending rule.
y-m-08-08.s.s3.line.1: From week1 to 3, grew 3cm each week.
y-m-08-08.s.s3.line.2: From week4, grew only 1 or 2cm weekly.
y-m-08-08.s.s3.line.3: So Seohyeon 30cm prediction with first rule may not be right for this bean.
y-m-08-08.s.s3.explain: Line5 overreaches. Growth 1cm weekly from week4 is based on only two intervals too. Same error: extending old 3-week rule to week10. Lines1-4 match data (9→11 is 2, 11→12 is 1).

y-m-08-04.title: Make number pattern whose fifth term 20
y-m-08-04.topic: Make pattern by adding same amount (design rule)
y-m-08-04.goal: Change starting number and increment to make different rules with same result; explain one grows as other shrinks.
y-m-08-04.material: Minho make pattern starting with first number then add same amount. Example start 2 add 3: 2,5,8,11,14,... Both first and increment natural numbers ≥1. He says only way fifth is 20: start 4, add 4 (4,8,12,16,20). 11 12 16 2 4 5 8 8
y-m-08-04.thinking.1: Describe paired change between two numbers
y-m-08-04.thinking.2: Reason how possible cases change as conditions change
y-m-08-04.prereq.1: Explain in words how pattern continues
y-m-08-04.s.s1.prompt: Wetin you think about wetin Minho talk? (First think and choose, then test am for next step.)
y-m-08-04.s.s1.hint.0: Write whether di fifth number really na 20 if first number na 4 and number wey you add na 4.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.hint.1: Use 1 as number to add, and think wetin first number gatz be for fifth number to be 20.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.o.a: E correct. 20 na multiple of 4, so na only first number and number to add be 4 and 4.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.r.a: Dis thinking only look say 20 multiple of 4 and choose same number for first number and number to add.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.o.b: No. You fit make 20 even if you change both.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.r.b: Dis thinking see say if you change both numbers together, you fit get same result.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.o.c: E correct. Fifth number depend only on number wey dem add, no matter wetin first number be.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.r.c: Dis thinking miss say fifth number depend on first number too.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.o.d: We no know yet. We gatz make several and test dem ourselves.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.r.d: Dis thinking wan test before e talk anything for sure.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.explain: If you change first number and number to add together, you fit make fifth number be 20 in plenty ways. Answer wey talk "I go test first, then talk" na good start too. Check by yourself for next step.
y-m-08-04.s.s1.acc.0: Holding judgment before testing na reasonable too. Test for next step then settle your judgment.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.prompt: Make three number patterns wey their fifth number na 20 and their number to add all different. a na first number and d na number to add.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.hint.0: Count how many times you need continue from first number to reach fifth number, and write am by yourself.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.hint.1: Choose number to add first, then reason backward wetin first number gatz be to make 20.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.ok.c1: First number and number to add na natural numbers 1 or more.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.fail.c1: Abeg make first number and number to add natural numbers wey be 1 or more.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.fail.c2: Fifth number no be 20. Write all numbers from first to fifth and check.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.explain: Four number patterns possible: (4, 4), (8, 3), (12, 2), (16, 1). Each time number to add go down by 1, first number go up by 4.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.prompt: If you make first number big, wetin happen to number to add? Explain with examples above.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.hint.0: Put number to add side by side when first number na 4 and when e na 16, then compare dem.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.hint.1: Since fifth number na di same, 20, think how both numbers gatz move.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.0: Di numbers for your example fit your explanation?
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.1: You connect why dem dey move opposite ways to result 20?
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.selfAssess.2: You check say your explanation fit all four cases?
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.model.0: If you make first number big, 16, number to add go small, 1. Di total must be 20, so dem dey move opposite ways.
y-m-08-04.s.s2.because.model.1: When starting number increase, number you gatz add each time decrease. Starting from 4 and adding 4 each time give 20, and starting from 8 and adding 3 each time give 20.
y-m-08-04.s.s3.prompt: You fit make fifth number 20 with number pattern wey first number na 6? (Number to add na natural number.)
y-m-08-04.s.s3.hint.0: Starting from first number 6, change number to add to 2, 3, and 4 and write fifth number.
y-m-08-04.s.s3.hint.1: Find boundary between numbers to add wey make fifth number smaller than 20 and ones wey make am bigger than 20.
y-m-08-04.s.s3.o.a: Impossible. Adding 3 each time give 18, and adding 4 each time give 22
y-m-08-04.s.s3.r.a: Dis idea try numbers to add one by one and find say dem skip 20.
y-m-08-04.s.s3.o.b: Possible. If number to add na 3.5, fifth number go be 20
y-m-08-04.s.s3.r.b: You extend am to decimals and calculate correctly, but for dis question number to add na natural number. Think again inside di condition.
y-m-08-04.s.s3.r.c: Conclusion na the same, but reason different. Even with different first number and different number to add, e fit become 20.
y-m-08-04.s.s3.o.d: Possible. If number to add na 2, fifth number go become 20
y-m-08-04.s.s3.r.d: Maybe na prediction wey you choose without calculating value after adding number four times. Start at 6 and write am yourself.
y-m-08-04.s.s3.explain: Starting from 6 and adding 3 each time give 6, 9, 12, 15, 18; adding 4 each time give 6, 10, 14, 18, 22. E no land on 20; e skip over am. You fit change number to add to 3.5, but with condition say na natural number, e impossible.

y-m-08-01.thinking.0: Finding the wrong line in a solution
y-m-08-01.title: Looking at tenth number Seojin found
y-m-08-01.topic: Find rule in number pattern (far term)
y-m-08-01.goal: Pair positions and values; see "increases by same amount" differs from "position times value"; fix wrong line to find tenth term.
y-m-08-01.material:
Seojin sees 1,3,5,7,9,... increasing by same amount each step, finds tenth term.
Position | 1st | 2nd | 3rd | 4th | 5th
Number | 1 | 3 | 5 | 7 | 9 1 3 5 7
y-m-08-01.thinking.3: Find same value in several ways
y-m-08-01.prereq.0: Tell next number after seeing pattern
y-m-08-01.s.s1.prompt: Choose line in Seojin solution hard to trust.
y-m-08-01.s.s1.hint.0: Put pair from line 2 into each statement one line at time.
y-m-08-01.s.s1.hint.1: Check each statement matches known pattern.
y-m-08-01.s.s1.line.0: Pattern grows by 2 each next number.
y-m-08-01.s.s1.line.2: When position increases 1, value increases 2, so multiply position by 2 to get value.
y-m-08-01.s.s1.explain: Line 3 first wrong. At position 1, ×2 gives 2 but actual first value 1. "Grows by 2" doesn't mean "position times 2." Line 4's 20 comes from wrong formula. Lines 1,2 match pattern. 1 2
y-m-08-01.s.s2.prompt: Choose all suitable ways to check Seojin method.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.hint.0: For each method ask "does it show Seojin answer wrong?"
y-m-08-01.s.s2.hint.1: Regardless of solver, how many methods can be checked using evidence?
y-m-08-01.s.s2.o.a: Assume Seojin correct and don't check
y-m-08-01.s.s2.r.a: This judges by person, but solution needs evidence.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.o.b: Write values one by one through tenth and compare to 20.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.r.b: This tests method directly. Takes time, but certain.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.o.c: Seojin say increase 2 each time, so treat line 3 method correct too
y-m-08-01.s.s2.r.c: This treat "increase 2" same as "multiply position by 2." Test with known values.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.o.d: Use line 3 method for 1st,2nd,3rd values and compare with actual.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.r.d: This apply method to values we already know.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.o.e: Pattern all odd, but 20 even, so wrong
y-m-08-01.s.s2.r.e: This use pattern property to say wrong, but no show how fix it.
y-m-08-01.s.s2.explain: You can test Seojin method on known pairs, write out through tenth and compare, or notice all terms odd but 20 even. Can't verify only because statements sound same or person said so.
y-m-08-01.s.s3.prompt: Make two pairs with different positions showing Seojin method (position×2) wrong. n natural 1 to 15, v nth term of 1,3,5,7,... 1 3 5 7
y-m-08-01.s.s3.hint.0: Continue pattern as far as needed.
y-m-08-01.s.s3.hint.1: Pair positions and values in table, compare with Seojin method result.
y-m-08-01.s.s3.fail.c2: v no be nth term. Continue pattern and check.
y-m-08-01.s.s3.ok.c3: Different from Seojin method. His method fail.
y-m-08-01.s.s3.explain: For example, 10th term na 19, not 20 (position×2). 6th term 11, not 12. At every position Seojin gives one more than actual. 1 2
y-m-08-01.s.s4.prompt: Tell Seojin correct way find tenth term. More than one method okay. 10
y-m-08-01.s.s4.hint.0: Think about fixing line 3 of solution.
y-m-08-01.s.s4.hint.1: After writing method, check it gives third term 5. 3
y-m-08-01.s.s4.selfAssess.0: You calculate whether your method gives 19?
y-m-08-01.s.s4.selfAssess.1: You point out wrong line before writing?
y-m-08-01.s.s4.selfAssess.2: You check another method also give 19?
y-m-08-01.s.s4.model.1: It is one less than position times 2. 10×2=20, minus 1 gives 19. 1

y-m-08-05.title: Finding same day of week on calendar
y-m-08-05.topic: Rule for when same day of week come again on calendar
y-m-08-05.goal: Use rule say same day of week come again every 7 days to find dates, and understand say di rule hold inside one month, but when month change, e depend on how many days di month get.
y-m-08-05.material: Dis na calendar for one month. Di month get 31 days, and di 3rd na Tuesday. Days of week dey order Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, and one week get 7 days. When one day pass, day of week move to next one.
y-m-08-05.thinking.0: Finding counting mistake for last conclusion of solution
y-m-08-05.thinking.1: Making several dates using di rule
y-m-08-05.thinking.2: Sorting out condition wey make di rule hold (number of days in month)
y-m-08-05.prereq.0: Order of day names, and fact say one week get 7 days
y-m-08-05.s.s1.prompt: Choose line for explanation below wey hard to believe.
y-m-08-05.s.s1.hint.0: Read each line and write all dates wey be Thursdays.
y-m-08-05.s.s1.hint.1: Count Thursday dates wey you write and compare whether each line fit dat result.
y-m-08-05.s.s1.line.0: Di 3rd na Tuesday, so di 5th na Thursday.
y-m-08-05.s.s1.line.1: Thursday dey come again every 7 days, so 12th, 19th, and 26th Thursdays too.
y-m-08-05.s.s1.line.2: Dis month get 31 days, so Thursday after 26th no dey inside dis month.
y-m-08-05.s.s1.line.3: So dis month get 5 Thursdays altogether.
y-m-08-05.s.s1.explain: Line 4 wrong. Thursdays wey you find for earlier lines na 5th, 12th, 19th, and 26th, wey be four days. Saying 5 count one too many. Lines 1 to 3 correct.
y-m-08-05.s.s2.prompt: Find three different dates for dis month wey be Saturdays. (d na date for dis month.)
y-m-08-05.s.s2.hint.0: Start from Tuesday 3rd, count days of week by moving one day at a time, and find when first Saturday be.
y-m-08-05.s.s2.hint.1: Once you find first Saturday, keep adding 7 and write dates wey no pass 31st.
y-m-08-05.s.s2.fail.c1: Dis month go from 1st to 31st. Abeg check di date.
y-m-08-05.s.s2.fail.c2: E no be Saturday. Count how many days from Tuesday 3rd to Saturday.
y-m-08-05.s.s2.explain: Di Saturdays na 7th, 14th, 21st, and 28th, 4 times. 7th, 4 days after Tuesday 3rd, na Saturday, and after dat e dey come every 7 days.
y-m-08-05.s.s3.prompt: Think of another month where di 3rd na Tuesday. If dat month get how many days, di 3rd for next month go be Tuesday too? (Think only months wey get 28, 30, or 31 days.)
y-m-08-05.s.s3.hint.0: Starting from Tuesday 3rd, write in order days of week after 7, 14, and 21 days pass, then look for pattern.
y-m-08-05.s.s3.hint.1: For each choice, write day of week after dat number of days and compare when e be the same weekday as Tuesday 3rd.
y-m-08-05.s.s3.r.a: You count how many places day of week shift after 30 days?
y-m-08-05.s.s3.r.b: Dis thinking look how many times 7 go inside number of days for month.
y-m-08-05.s.s3.r.c: Dis thinking assume say after one month, same date go be same day of week.
y-m-08-05.s.s3.o.d: E always be the same no matter how many days di month get.
y-m-08-05.s.s3.r.d: Dis thinking assume weekday same even when number of days different by month.
y-m-08-05.s.s3.explain: 28 days after Tuesday 3rd na 4 times 7 days, so e Tuesday again. After 30 days, two more days pass, so e Thursday; after 31 days, three more days pass, so e Friday.
y-m-08-05.s.s4.prompt: For month where di 3rd na Tuesday, write why weekday for 3rd of next month depend on how many days dat month get.
y-m-08-05.s.s4.hint.0: When month get 28 days and when e get 31 days, split number of days until 3rd of next month into groups of 7 days.
y-m-08-05.s.s4.hint.1: Think say if any days remain after making groups, weekday go move that many places.
y-m-08-05.s.s4.selfAssess.0: You talk how many times 28 days contain 7 days?
y-m-08-05.s.s4.selfAssess.1: You talk how many places weekday move when e get 30 or 31 days?
y-m-08-05.s.s4.selfAssess.2: Using your explanation, you check say weekday 31 days later na Friday?
y-m-08-05.s.s4.model.0: 28 days na 4 times 7 days, so e fit exactly and weekday na the same. With 30 days, 2 days remain, so e become weekday two days later, Thursday.
y-m-08-05.s.s4.model.1: With 31 days, 4 weeks (28 days) pass, and 3 more days add, so e become Friday, 3 days after Tuesday.
y-m-08-05.s.s4.model.2: E be same day of week only when number of days na multiple of 7. 28 multiple of 7, but 30 and 31 no be.

y-m-08-06.title: Comparing two shops to buy pencils
y-m-08-06.topic: Comparing how two amounts change together (price and number)
y-m-08-06.goal: Compare two relationships with different starting values and amounts of increase, realize say which shop cheaper depend on how many you buy, and recommend one with reason.
y-m-08-06.material:
You wan buy pencils. Prices for two shops be like dis.
Shop 가: One pencil cost 500원.
Shop 나: First pencil cost 700원, and each extra pencil increase price by 400원. (Example: 2 pencils cost 700원+400원.)
Assume number of pencils you buy dey between 1 and 10.
y-m-08-06.thinking.0: Noticing say answer depend on conditions
y-m-08-06.thinking.1: Finding several numbers wey fit conditions
y-m-08-06.thinking.3: Stating comparison result together with reason
y-m-08-06.prereq.0: Calculating with natural numbers in 원 (Grade 3 level)
y-m-08-06.prereq.1: Comparing two values side by side in table
y-m-08-06.s.s1.prompt: If you still no know how many pencils you go buy, which shop cheaper?
y-m-08-06.s.s1.hint.0: Write in table prices for 1, 2, and 3 pencils for each shop.
y-m-08-06.s.s1.hint.1: Compare how much each shop price increase each time pencil number go up by one.
y-m-08-06.s.s1.o.a: Shop 가 cheaper, because price of one pencil cheaper.
